title: Perf Canary Dashboards (Inventory, Links, and Usage Guide)
author: Felix Schneider
content:
## Purpose
This page is the canonical inventory of Grafana dashboards used by the production performance-regression canary ("perf-canary"). It also documents:
- What each dashboard answers (p95 latency vs tokens/sec, slice comparisons, attribution)
- How to use the standard filters (model / region / gpu_sku / runtime_build / scheduler_mode)
- How deploy annotations are generated and how to correlate regressions with runtime releases
- Where to click next during triage (alerts → panels → runbook)

These dashboards are intended for Runtime, SRE, and Telemetry triage during canary rollout and ongoing operations. They are not customer-facing.

---

## Access and prerequisites
**Grafana folder:** `Engineering / Perf Canary`

**Data sources:**
- `prometheus-prod` (metrics)
- `tempo-prod` (traces, request exemplars when available)
- `loki-prod` (optional logs, used in a few drill-down links)

**RBAC:** If you cannot see the folder, request access via `INT-3321` (internal helpdesk) or file a new ticket under `Internal Support → Observability Access`.

---

## Quick start (triage workflow)
1) Open **[PC-00] Perf Canary — Overview** and set the global filters:
   - `region` (start with the paged region)
   - `model` (from alert payload)
   - `gpu_sku` (match alert payload; if unknown, pick `*` first)
2) Confirm the signal quality:
   - check sample counts and canary request rate
   - check warmup/priming indicators
3) Correlate with deploy annotations:
   - look for `runtime_build` / `git_sha` annotations near the inflection
4) Use **[PC-10] Model Detail** to isolate the regression dimension:
   - compare across `gpu_sku` and `scheduler_mode`
   - inspect batch composition panels
5) If regression is real and sustained, follow the runbook:
   - `runbook-perf-canary-regression-triage` (linked in every dashboard header)

---

## Standard dashboard variables (filters)
All dashboards in this folder share the same variable schema to keep triage consistent.

**Global variables:**
- `env`: `prod` (locked for this folder)
- `region`: e.g., `us-east`, `eu-west` (multi-select enabled on most dashboards)
- `model`: canonical serving model name (e.g., `llama-3.1-70b-instruct`, `qwen2.5-72b-instruct`)
- `streaming`: `true|false` (where applicable; some dashboards show both as separate panels)
- `gpu_sku`: e.g., `h100-sxm`, `h100-pcie`, `a100-80gb` (exact naming per Telemetry spec)
- `runtime_build`: Redwood runtime build identifier (release train + build number; example: `runtime-2026.02.12-rc3`)
- `git_sha`: runtime git SHA (used mainly for annotation correlation)
- `scheduler_mode`: e.g., `pinned_v1`, `default`, `canary_pinned_no_heuristic_x` (names follow runtime instrumentation)

**Notes on filtering:**
- If you multi-select `runtime_build`, the charts may become busy; prefer single-build selection when comparing.
- If `gpu_sku=*` hides a GPU-specific issue, use **[PC-21] GPU SKU Heatmap** to identify which SKU diverges first.

---

## Dashboard inventory

### [PC-00] Perf Canary — Overview (p95 + tokens/sec)
**Primary use:** First stop from a page. Confirms whether the alert is real and identifies the most likely regression dimension.

**Link:** https://grafana.prod.redwoodinference.com/d/pc00-perf-canary-overview
**UID:** `pc00`

**Key panels:**
- *p95 end-to-end latency (ms)* by `model` (top N) and by selected `model`
- *tokens/sec* (decode throughput) split by `streaming=true/false`
- *first-token latency p95* (streaming)
- *canary request rate* + *sample size per window*
- *error rate* (HTTP, model-level failures)
- *batch composition summary* (prefill/decode counts, max seq len)

**Annotations enabled:**
- Runtime deploys (release train events)
- Canary runner deploys
- Maintenance windows / suppression windows

**Screenshot (reference):** https://docs.redwoodinference.com/internal/perf-canary/screenshots/pc00-overview-2026-02-16.png

---

### [PC-10] Perf Canary — Model Detail (slice comparison)
**Primary use:** Isolate the regression to a slice: `gpu_sku`, `scheduler_mode`, `runtime_build`, `streaming`.

**Link:** https://grafana.prod.redwoodinference.com/d/pc10-perf-canary-model-detail
**UID:** `pc10`

**Key panels:**
- *p50/p95/p99 latency* (ms) for selected `model`, with optional split by `gpu_sku`
- *tokens/sec p50/p95* for selected `model`
- *prefill latency vs decode latency* (when instrumentation is available)
- *KV cache hit rate* and *KV cache evictions* (canary-tagged)
- *scheduler queue depth* and *time in queue* (canary request class)
- *kernel selection distribution* (selected kernel id) + *fallback reason counts* (gated behind canary tag)

**Triage hints (embedded in dashboard as text panel):**
- If latency regresses without tokens/sec change, suspect queueing/scheduling or first-token path.
- If tokens/sec regresses with stable latency, suspect decode kernel / quantization path / batch composition drift.
- If only one `gpu_sku` regresses, check recent driver/firmware changes or SKU-specific kernel selection.

**Screenshot (reference):** https://docs.redwoodinference.com/internal/perf-canary/screenshots/pc10-model-detail-2026-02-16.png

---

### [PC-21] Perf Canary — GPU SKU Heatmap (fleet heterogeneity)
**Primary use:** Identify which GPU SKU(s) are driving a region/model regression, and catch silent heterogeneity issues.

**Link:** https://grafana.prod.redwoodinference.com/d/pc21-perf-canary-gpu-heatmap
**UID:** `pc21`

**Key panels:**
- *p95 latency heatmap* (y = `gpu_sku`, x = time)
- *tokens/sec heatmap* (y = `gpu_sku`, x = time)
- *sample count heatmap* (ensures heatmap is meaningful; low samples are faded)
- *runtime_build by gpu_sku* (shows mixed fleets during rollout)

**How to read:**
- A “stripe” indicates a SKU-specific regression.
- A vertical shift across all SKUs usually indicates runtime build change or telemetry pipeline change.

---

### [PC-30] Perf Canary — Deploy Correlation (annotations + diffs)
**Primary use:** Confirm timing against runtime deploys and capture the precise build window for rollback/bisect.

**Link:** https://grafana.prod.redwoodinference.com/d/pc30-perf-canary-deploy-correlation
**UID:** `pc30`

**Key panels:**
- *p95 latency* with dense deploy annotations and build labels
- *tokens/sec* with the same annotations
- *runtime_build rollout coverage* (percentage of canary requests by build)
- *deploy diff links* (static links constructed from annotation payload)

**Deploy annotation sources:**
- `runtime-release-annotations` (from Release Engineering)
- `perf-canary-runner-deploy` (runner service)

**Useful links (from within dashboard):**
- Runtime compare: https://github.com/redwoodinference/redwood/compare/${PREV_SHA}...${CUR_SHA}
- Release notes: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/eng-serving-runtime/Runtime+Release+Notes

---

### [PC-40] Perf Canary — Alert Drilldown (what paged and why)
**Primary use:** Match the detector output to what you see on charts (baseline, regression ratio, sample size).

**Link:** https://grafana.prod.redwoodinference.com/d/pc40-perf-canary-alert-drilldown
**UID:** `pc40`

**Key panels:**
- *regression score vs baseline* (ratio and absolute delta)
- *baseline value* (rolling median or pinned known-good; see ADR-0231)
- *minimum sample size satisfied?* (binary + counts)
- *suppression status* (deploy window / maintenance window)
- *dedup key preview* (matches PagerDuty grouping)

---

### [PC-50] Perf Canary — Canary Runner Health (safety + overhead)
**Primary use:** Ensure the canary runner is not causing production harm and is producing stable measurements.

**Link:** https://grafana.prod.redwoodinference.com/d/pc50-perf-canary-runner-health
**UID:** `pc50`

**Key panels:**
- Runner request QPS (rate-limited), success rate, retries
- Runner CPU/memory, event loop lag
- Per-model schedule adherence (skips, backoff)
- Canary “safe class” priority metrics (confirm it is not stealing capacity)

**Operational note:** If runner health is degraded, pause paging and file an issue under the perf-canary Linear epic; do not treat latency shifts as runtime regressions until sampling is stable.

---

## Panel conventions and metric naming
These dashboards assume the metrics and labels from the metric spec page. In brief:
- Latency is reported as *end-to-end request latency* and (where available) *first-token latency*.
- Throughput is reported as *tokens/sec* for decode; streaming and non-streaming are separated.
- Canary traffic is filtered via `source="perf-canary"` and `request_class="canary_safe"`.

**Common pitfalls:**
- Mixed `runtime_build` within a time window can blur p95 changes. Prefer splitting by `runtime_build` or use the rollout coverage panel.
- Low samples during warmup/priming can produce misleading p95 swings. Always check sample count panels.

---

## Deploy annotations: what they mean
Deploy annotations appear as vertical markers with a tooltip including:
- `runtime_build`
- `git_sha`
- `region`
- `rollout_stage` (e.g., `canary`, `25%`, `100%`)
- optional `change_summary` (short)

**When to trust an annotation correlation:**
- The regression starts within ~1–2 aggregation windows of the annotation.
- Rollout coverage indicates a significant fraction of canary requests moved to the new `runtime_build`.
- The shift is visible in at least one stable slice (single GPU SKU / pinned scheduler mode).
